body.x: Noogi (CEO Park Chanwook) has announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company will showcase its first AI-integrated ergonomic chair, “N Signature,” at the “K-Startup Pavilion.” Specializing in ergonomic chairs tailored to individual body types and conditions, Noogi has been working to raise awareness about the importance of proper sitting posture for spinal health.

The N Signature goes beyond traditional seating solutions by offering adjustable components to suit users’ height and body structure, promoting the healthiest and most comfortable sitting posture. Its innovative six-segment tilting backrest technology independently adjusts within three seconds of sitting, ensuring optimal balance and posture. Collaborative research between Noogi and a university lab, analyzing data from 100 participants, demonstrated the chair’s superiority over competitors in maintaining lumbar curvature and balance and reducing muscle fatigue by up to 55%.

body.cap: Noogi’s healthcare solution and AI-IoT chair, ‘N’ Signature. | Photo by Noogi

body.x: The chair’s ergonomic design also minimizes pressure on the hamstrings, supporting better blood circulation and preventing crossed-leg sitting habits that can lead to pelvic misalignment and musculoskeletal disorders. Additionally, the N Signature monitors users’ posture in real-time and sends notifications via a connected smartphone or smartwatch app when corrections are needed. It offers tailored exercise content and gym ball-compatible features to support comprehensive health management.

“N Signature is more than an AI chair—it’s a next-generation IoT solution that supports healthy lifestyles,” a Noogi representative said. “Through its CES debut, we aim to showcase the potential of cutting-edge healthcare systems and their functionality to a global audience.”

The representative added, “We are targeting the U.S., a hub for healthcare and research. We are proposing the ‘N’ Signature to reduce the financial burden of medical services for locals. During CES, we plan to engage with U.S.-based medical professionals specializing in spinal and cervical health, pursuing collaborative research and validation to expand sales opportunities.”

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
